subject: physics_2
question_text: Write the truth table of NAND gate. How does it differ from AND gate?

mark_split.label: Truth table of the NAND gate

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. TRANSCRIPTION: the space before the question mark in the printed question is dropped. Truth table hand-checked against the book (p.55) row by row — 00→1, 10→1, 01→1, 11→0 — and against the definition NAND = AND followed by NOT. The rows are written one per line rather than as a ruled grid, because the notebook is set in a proportional handwriting font in which spaced columns do not stay aligned. The output symbol needs an overbar, which Unicode does not encode honestly, so that line is authored as KaTeX.

recall_prompt: Give the four rows of the NAND truth table, then say how its output differs from the AND gate's.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: NAND truth table
steps.margin_note: First mark. All four rows, and only the last row has output 0.
steps.why: A NAND gate is an AND gate followed by a NOT gate, so its output column is the AND column turned upside down. The AND column is 0, 0, 0, 1 and the NAND column is 1, 1, 1, 0.
common_mistakes: Writing the AND column by mistake — 0, 0, 0, 1 instead of 1, 1, 1, 0.
Leaving out the bar over A · B. Without the bar the expression is the AND gate.

recall.must_convey: That the NAND output is 1 for the first three input pairs and 0 only when both inputs are 1.
accept: output is zero only when both inputs are one
high except for the last row

steps.memory_tip: Three ones then a zero — the AND column written backwards.

steps.label: Difference from AND
steps.mark_note: NAND output is the inverse of AND
lines: The output of an AND gate is 1 only when
The output of a NAND gate is 0 only when
both inputs are 1; it is 1 for every other

lines.text: NAND output = inverse of the AND output

steps.margin_note: Second mark. State both gates, then say one output is the inverse of the other.
steps.why: Naming the difference row by row is slow and easy to get wrong. Saying that NAND is an AND gate followed by a NOT gate gives the same information in one line and is the reason the two columns are opposite.
common_mistakes: Saying only that the outputs are different. The examiner looks for the word inverse, or for AND followed by NOT.
Saying the inputs differ. The inputs are the same; only the output column is inverted.

recall.must_convey: That the NAND output is the inverse of the AND output, so NAND is 0 only when both inputs are 1.
accept: NAND is AND followed by NOT
AND is high only for one one, NAND is low only for one one
reject: output is one one one zero

steps.memory_tip: NAND = AND + NOT. The N in front means the output is turned over.

insider_note: The table alone is one mark. The second mark needs the word inverse — or the sentence NAND is an AND gate followed by a NOT gate.
